title: ExecutionPermit
description: Final admitted action digest, enforcement grade, adapter, constraints, expiry and single-use nonce (plan: 'Wire contracts'). Schema only — E0 defines this shape; issuing one (deciding admission) is E2 scope. The plan's single-use nonce IS the envelope's nonce field; there is no second nonce. Platform names never enter this schema (plan: 'Host adapters') — adapter is a free identifier of an adapter class (e.g. 'subprocess'), not a product name. `aud`/`cnf` (quick win 5, RFC 7800 `cnf`/DPoP-style) sender-constrain the permit to one executor identity and one confirmed key; both are OPTIONAL so an unconstrained permit stays schema-valid, but `wire.executor.consume_and_execute` requires both together, plus a verified proof of possession, the moment either is present. `governance_block_digest` (quick win 9) is the RFC 8785 digest of the GovernanceBlock the admission ruling actually used, pinned here so a host can check it against a signed, trust-store-authorized policy author's digest.

enforcement_grade.description: plan: only mediated/platform are enforcement; advisory may be ignored by the caller

constraints.description: lane/lock/drift bindings and any other admission-time constraint; free-form, host- and adapter-defined

aud.description: the intended executor/adapter identity this permit is bound to (RFC 7800-style audience); OPTIONAL, but required together with cnf for a sender-constrained permit

jkt.description: RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint (SHA-256, base64url) of the executor's Ed25519 public key, as an RFC 8037 OKP JWK (crv, kty, x)

cnf.description: RFC 7800 confirmation claim; OPTIONAL, but required together with aud for a sender-constrained permit

governance_block_digest.description: RFC 8785 digest of the GovernanceBlock this permit's admission ruling was decided under (quick win 9); OPTIONAL -- present only when admission was given a signed, pinned governance block
